cohort: The study included a weighted sample of 544,930 teen mothers, 19 years of age and younger, from Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System data collected between 2012 and 2016.
finding: Racial/ethnic differences were observed in the receipt of perinatal counseling, with non-Hispanic black teens more likely to receive counseling on substance use and HIV testing, and Hispanic teens more likely to receive influenza vaccine recommendations compared to non-Hispanic white teens.
cross-section timing: Data was collected on both prenatal and postnatal counseling.
